Cutting out the Middleman

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Social apps like Uber and Airbnb apps cutting out the middleman

Summary:
The ultimate success for a business has always been when you can sell directly to your customer this used to mean the Avon lady or the equivalent, now the internet, social media, the incredible success and speed of new apps on the market has made this go direct, a reality in the world of big business.

Uber Taxi’s is the biggest taxi company in the world today BUT they don’t own any cars.
Airbnb is the biggest hotel chain in the world today but it doesn’t own any hotel/properties.

Uber taxi’s and Airbnb are arguably the biggest companies disrupting traditional business,,,,

Technplogy has made them able to put consumers directly in touch with supplier.


With Toby Shapshack, social media and tech guru we will look at the different tools that have become the new norm to book and use a service. These are tools that are cutting hidden costs, empowering the consumers and cutting the middle man something Toby is passionate about.

With Andy Rice, creative brand strategist, we will explore what this means on how business today markets and brands themselves…how do they compete with the giant of social media, how do they adapt and NOT die.


Further information:
We will take on reality style this new economic friendly ways of living, of getting from A to B, of hiring people, of having holidays, of buying and selling.

We will take a ride in an uber taxi, interview this new entrepreneur how does he make his money, is this a new income, what does uber guarantee them these ride and drive entrepreneurs…Bashir who was a tour guides has found this new line of work a great source of income. He averages, R 1000.00 a day profit and will work until late to maintain this, but still manage to pick up his son in the middle of the day.

How has Uber impacted on the car rental companies, and have they these companies managed to adapt?

Uber now operates in 10 sub-Saharan African cities, whose local taxi companies and start ups have been working hard to compete with them but so far the ride hailing company has managed to outmanoeuvre most of them. This could change as Safaricom East Africa’s largest mobile phone network is launching a competive option in Kenya called Little Cabs. This will be Uber’s first real challenge.

Samantha Allenberg, spokesperson for Uber Africa is all for consumer choice and competition.
“We do not focus on competitors but rather spend our time thinking about how we can better the experience for riders and driver-partners. However, Uber loves choice as it creates competition and a better experience for the consumers.”

But are smaller competitors getting better at competing and distinguishing themselves fro Uber especially as Uber drivers face protests, intimidation, and in some cases violence..

The internet travel booking service Airbnb has become a major income earner for thousands of South African’s. Local hosts are earning on average R 28 000 a year as tourists are making South Africa a travel destination.

Nicola D’Elia, managing director for Africa and Middle East at Airbnb. Has said the company has reported 190% growth in local hosts to 7 500 with 134 000 inbound guests, representing growth of 250%, and guests staying an average of 4.9 nights.
“If you look at the numbers, on average last summer we had one million guests travelling on Airbnb every single day. Our community is based on trust and safety is paramount for us,”
How have they stayed ahead of the game…how do they ensure quality one of the ways is they only allow reviews from guests and hosts who have booked with each other.
The depreciation of the rand has made SA more attractive to foreign visitors who make up 72% of the local Airbnb visitors.

Key diff Uber and Abnb are aggregators not only to they have a ready supply of service providers they enable you to complete a transaction within seconds without credit card…

Don’t advertise, everything word of mouth via social media

What has made Uber possible it has linked a data base of cars owners with google maps and google maps is the equivalent of the taxi meter in working out the fare and it can tell you in advance

Andy Rice Creative and Brand Strategist

Mr. Toby Shapshak Innovation & technology analyst
Mr. Vuyisa Qabaka Mentor:Entrepreneur

Press Release:


No Assets Required :
Uber doesn’t own a single taxi yet it’s taken this industry by storm. Airbnb doesn’t own a single hotel or bed but has done the same in that sector. From planning a holiday to shopping and more, Carte Blanche reports on app-based disruptive technologies pushing out the known middleman and cashing in on direct-to-consumer services and assets they don’t own.


Script:


Link
Aah Cape Town, It’s the perfect destination for any one looking for some good sun even some good wine but for poor souls like me its all about work but whatever your reason for coming here to get transport from the airport to your destination is as easy as a tap of your button.

V/O 8 sec
Uber …operating in South Africa since 2014 …is turning the taxi industry upside down …. disruptive business at its best.

Toby Shapshak: Disruption is this fancy catch phrase that every one uses or innovation basically what it is, is that the old way of doing things is being changed its being disrupted by more efficient ways.

V/O 6 sec
Toby Shapshak, tech guru and Editor of Stuff….a magazine bursting with the latest tech toys.

Toby Shapshak: In the past you had to book through a taxi company who took their share of the profits Uber has short-circuited that by allowing you to connect with one of their drivers.

Bongani: In a way its an old model its all about cutting out the middle man?
Toby: Exactly and the middle man for the longest time has been where the profit centre was. If you speak to a recording artist most of the money went to the record label now because of the ability for anybody to contact anybody else through a mobile device you don’t need the infrastructure that used to exist before.

Link: Ubers numbers are already staggering over 10 million users world wide have taken over a billion rides in over 400 cities.

V/O 6 sec
At its core Uber is a software tool, for connecting drivers with people looking for a ride.

Andy Rice: It’s a great example of people discovering to their cost that competition comes from an unexpected source.

V/O 3 sec
Andy Rice is a creative brand strategist.

Andy: You wouldn’t have expected as taxi driver to face severe competition from an organisation that didn’t own a single taxi. What Uber really capitalised on was an understanding what the consumer the customer looks for in a service and in many respects I believe Uber has grown the market just as much as it has replaced traditionally taxi operations.

V/O 10 sec
Air B&B another pioneer disruptive business that’s impacted the hotel industry …..sharing your space through a data base … it all started with a problem…..

Link: 9 years ago two young designers Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia couldn’t afford the rent on their San Francisco apartment. To make ends meet, they decided to turn their loft into place to rent but they didn’t even have a bed so they had to go out and get an air mattress and that’s how AB&B was born.

Andy Rice: Even the name gives a clue to how flimsy the proposition was when they first started, they battled for some time, I think all of these things take time to achieve critical mass where they get recommendations starting to go through social media.

Vuyisa : We are in the middle of this great revolution even country borders don’t matter because we are now digital nomads our work follows us and not the other way around.

V/O
Vuyisa Qabaka is at the fore front of change in the way we work…mentoring entrepreneurs and start up’s.

Vuyisa: Environments like this really help facilitate the free flow of ideas dynamic people doing great things and shifting the world. Creating a place where there are no walls where people can see one another and have conversations ….

Toby: And suddenly we have the power and not the big companies and that’s the persuasive theme about this internet economy that us consumers have more power than we are used to when things were run by big corporations.

V/O
Uber is the largest taxi company in the world yet it doesn’t own a single taxi….
Airbnb the biggest hotel company globally and they don’t own any properties.

Toby Shapshak: 1 million people a night in 1.4 million homes around the world and it doesn’t own 1 bed if that doesn’t tell you that disruption is going to radically change the business status quoi nothing else will.

LINK
Airbnb has become a major income earner for thousands of South African’s who have turned apartments, spare rooms, high profile properties into viable income earners….Cape Town is a prime location…

V/O
And the mother city has been good to Airbnb host Mary Baily.

Bongani : … and look at this view WOW

Bongani: What attracted you to Airbnb?
Mary: I love CT, I love property and I had heard from a friend that it could be quiet successful I looked at my house to start off you really have to be quiet critical of your own space I made it look really good and all of a sudden I was getting tons of bookings through Airbnb.
Bongani: What about the idea of strangers in your intimate space?
Being in property I look at property as an investment it’s about sharing, sharing your personal space with people you don’t know. I have had the most amazing people staying in our home and staying in apartments.

V/O 10 sec
Traditional, taxi drivers have rioted in protest against Uber not only in Johannesburg and Cape Town but also earlier this year in Paris, France…

Bongani: What happens when big business don’t innovate?
Toby Shapshak: if you don’t cannibalise your self as Steve Jobs so famously said somebody else will the taxi industry seemed set never to be attacked by anyone else until along came this little SF company and the next thing they are on the back foot why? Because they didn’t innovate they didn’t disrupt their own their own business model,

V/O 4 sec
Kodak is a prime example of a company that didn’t adapt.

Bongani: Kodak disappeared even though they invented digital photography
Vuyisa: This is exactly it you can find many patents of large companies who think that innovation is something you write a patent about and put in your safe and one day some how it will become relevant all of this has changed a business in the technology environment can go from zero to multi billion in under 2 years, reality of the world we live in today.

Andy Rice: Go back to Uber it was a clever creative piece of technology development that made it possible and it is only those who have their heads in the sand like an ostrich who say I wont respond you have to respond or you are out of business.

V/O 13 sec
But it’s not all have an idea, have an app and the rest is history… Airbnb took a while before coming up with the winning formula…Mary has expanded … but it’s been hard work

Mary: I just invested in another property and then another and we have now got 4, the money to invest didn’t really come out of the profits of the Airbnb. It does make you money you have just got to be clever in investing and then turning them into beautiful spaces.

V/O 10 sec
Technology is changing the concept of work and what a job is, …unless South Africa keeps pace millions, will be left behind.

Vuyisa: Its estimated 67% of current jobs in our market can be replaced by machines or by some form of technology and that’s a massive drain potential in the country some of the brightest and smartest ideas I have had the pleasure of engaging with are coming from this continent,,, the challenge from the government is they are not providing infrastructure fast enough they are not closing the digital gap at the right rapid place so we need our government and leaders to be more in tune with where the future is going.

LINK
The most fundamental principle of disruption is actually quiet old fashioned it’s the idea for business’s to work they must solve a problem and right now someone somewhere is having a light bulb moment
